ai.definition: Lunar bases are facilities established on the Moon to support human habitation and scientific research. They serve as testbeds for technologies that could be used in more distant space exploration.
ai.howItWorks: Lunar bases require a combination of habitats, power generation, life support systems, communication infrastructure, and robotic systems to facilitate sustained human presence. These facilities can leverage the Moon's resources, such as regolith and water ice, for construction and life support.
ai.problemSolved: Reducing the logistical burden of long-duration space missions by providing a closer staging point from which to launch further exploration or habitation efforts in deep space.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing processes involve developing lightweight, durable materials that can withstand lunar conditions. This includes constructing habitats using regolith as a building material and sourcing water ice for life support systems.
ai.buildProcess: The construction of lunar bases involves robotic missions to gather resources, followed by the deployment of human crews to assemble and operate the facilities. Initial stages may include small-scale prototypes before scaling up to full-fledged operational bases.
ai.costDrivers: High initial investment in technology development, transportation costs for equipment and crew, and ongoing maintenance expenses. Cost drivers also include the complexity of establishing a self-sustaining environment on an extraterrestrial body.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is promising but faces significant technological and financial challenges. Successful implementation could lead to broader space exploration efforts, but it requires substantial investment and international cooperation.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations governing the construction of lunar bases, though international agreements like the Outer Space Treaty provide a framework for responsible space activity.
ai.risks: Technological risks include developing reliable life support systems and power generation in harsh lunar environments. Operational risks involve crew safety and health during extended stays on the Moon. Financial risks stem from high initial costs and potential delays in funding.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain due to the high initial investment required, but successful lunar bases could lead to spin-off technologies and new markets for space resources.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving life support systems, developing more efficient ways of extracting resources from the Moon, and enhancing communication capabilities between Earth and the Moon.

glossary.def: A layer of loose, heterogeneous surface material on planetary bodies, including the Moon.
An international agreement signed in 1967 that governs the exploration and use of outer space by all nations.

subsystems.name: Landing and ascent system
subsystems.role: delivers cargo and crews to the surface and returns them to orbit.

subsystems.name: Habitat and pressure shell
subsystems.role: keeps people alive at breathable pressure against vacuum.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: runs habitat, instruments and processing through the 14-day lunar night.

subsystems.name: Life support and resource processing
subsystems.role: recycles air and water and extracts oxygen and water from local rock and ice.

subsystems.name: Construction and surface works
subsystems.role: builds landing pads, roads and shielding without hauling material from Earth.

subsystems.name: Communications and navigation
subsystems.role: links surface crews to orbit and Earth and fixes positions for precision landing.

buildSteps.title: Find the site
buildSteps.detail: Target a polar ridge with near-continuous sunlight for power, standing beside permanently shadowed craters that hold water ice. Orbital and impactor missions have already mapped likely ice deposits.

buildSteps.title: Send robotic precursors
buildSteps.detail: Rovers and small landers prospect the ice, measure soil strength and radiation, and prove precision landing in long-shadow terrain before people commit.

buildSteps.title: Land power and communications first
buildSteps.detail: Cargo landers set down solar arrays, batteries, a fission power unit and a relay antenna so later missions arrive at a working site rather than an empty one.

buildSteps.title: Emplace a pressure shell
buildSteps.detail: A rigid or inflatable habitat module is landed and connected, then covered with regolith or sandbags to cut radiation and thermal swings.

buildSteps.title: Start resource extraction
buildSteps.detail: Excavated icy regolith is heated to release water; electrolysis splits it into oxygen for breathing and hydrogen for propellant. Oxygen can also be freed from dry regolith by molten-oxide electrolysis.

buildSteps.title: Build in place
buildSteps.detail: Regolith is sintered or printed into blocks for landing pads, berms and shelters, so mass lifted from Earth falls for every later phase.

buildSteps.title: Commission with a crew
buildSteps.detail: A short crewed stay presses the habitat up, checks recycling and power, and verifies that dust control and repairs actually work in person.

buildSteps.title: Extend the base
buildSteps.detail: Add modules, a greenhouse for some food, a propellant depot and spare landing pads, turning a camp into infrastructure for missions further out.

prerequisites.why: robotic landers have reached the surface, but ton-scale soft landings and crewed ascent from the Moon are still being developed.
orbiters and impactor missions show ice exists in polar cold traps, but nobody has mined or processed it on the surface.
regolith oxygen extraction has been demonstrated in laboratories and ground test beds, not in flight.

prerequisites.tech: Surface power through the lunar night
prerequisites.why: solar plus batteries struggles over 14 days of darkness, so small fission reactors are being designed and tested for surface use.
no atmosphere means galactic cosmic rays and solar storms arrive unshielded, and abrasive dust fouls seals, joints and lungs.

pathway.milestone: robotic landers and orbital reconnaissance, with a staged crewed programme building toward surface landings
pathway.unlocks: a map of where ice, sunlight and trafficable ground coincide.

pathway.milestone: first crewed surface stays of days to weeks from a small station in lunar orbit
pathway.unlocks: operational experience with regolith, dust and surface power.

pathway.milestone: an Antarctic-style polar outpost with oxygen and water made on site
pathway.unlocks: stays of months rather than days, and a large cut in resupply mass from Earth.

pathway.milestone: permanent base, propellant depot and landing pads built from local material
pathway.unlocks: a staging point where spacecraft can refuel before heading to Mars or to asteroids.
